query: meta-agent modifies training environment during multi-turn reinforcement learning
text:
1. **[EAU: Environment-Agent-User Co-evolution for Training User-Centric Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16523)** — October 2026. **Closest match:** a meta-agent monitors multi-turn RL training and modifies the environment, user simulator, rewards, and training configuration; validated changes are applied during the ongoing run. **People:** Min Cai (University of Alberta), Dan Zhang (National University of Singapore), Gao Xing and Libin Ma (Kuaishou Technology), Zhaohui Xu (independent researcher), and Xi Ye (University of Alberta; Amii).

2. **[Weak-for-Strong: Training Weak Meta-Agent to Harness Strong Executors](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.04785)** — April 2025. Related work that trains a smaller meta-agent with multi-turn RL to iteratively design and improve workflows for stronger models. Its focus is workflow optimization, rather than modifying a live training environment. **People:** Fan Nie, Haotian Ye, Weixin Liang, Pan Lu, and James Zou (Stanford University); Lan Feng and Alexandre Alahi (EPFL); Huaxiu Yao (UNC–Chapel Hill).

query: adaptive user simulator reward design LLM agents
text:
1. **[UserLM-R1: Modeling Human Reasoning in User Language Models with Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.09215)** (2026). Closely matches the query: dynamic user profiles, strategic decision-making, and rewards for consistency, reasoning quality, and resistance to manipulation. **People:** Feng Zhang, Shijia Li, Chunmao Zhang, Zhanyu Ma, Jun Xu, Jiuchong Gao, Jinghua Hao, Renqing He, Jingwen Xu, and Han Liu. **Affiliations:** Meituan, Peking University, Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, and Dalian University of Technology.

2. **[UserRL: Training Interactive User-Centric Agent via Reinforcement Learning](https://lifelongagent.github.io/Project-Lifelong-Agent/UserRL/index.html)** (2025). Studies how turn-level rewards and whole-conversation scoring affect agents trained against simulated users. **People:** Cheng Qian and Heng Ji (**University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign**); Zuxin Liu, Akshara Prabhakar, Jielin Qiu, Zhiwei Liu, Haolin Chen, Shirley Kokane, Weiran Yao, Shelby Heinecke, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, and Huan Wang (**Salesforce AI Research**).

3. **[Learning User Simulators with Turing Rewards](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19336)** (2026). Trains simulators using an LLM judge’s assessment of whether responses are indistinguishable from a real user’s, conditioned on their history. **People:** Yingshan Susan Wang, Cedegao E. Zhang, Linlu Qiu, Zexue He, Pengyuan Li, Alex Pentland, Roger P. Levy, and Yoon Kim. **Affiliations:** MIT, Stanford University, and MIT–IBM Watson AI Lab.

4. **[What does it take to build a human-like user simulator?](https://nickatomlin.github.io/blog/user-simulators-2.html)** (2025). Accessible research overview covering simulator context, interaction scaffolds, training objectives, and how user preferences should translate into rewards. **People:** Jessy Lin (**UC Berkeley**) and Nicholas Tomlin (**NYU at publication; now Toyota Technological Institute at Chicago**). [Affiliation context](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/nyu-center-for-data-science_usersimulators-airesearch-humancomputerinteraction-activity-7397736121931091968-Smzf).

query: within-run and across-run adaptation agent training
text:
1. **[A-SR: Self-Evolving Agentic LLMs for Symbolic Regression via Hierarchical Coordination](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04872)** — The closest match: explicitly distinguishes **within-run adaptation** of roles and memory, with frozen model weights, from **across-run training** through trajectory distillation and LoRA. **People:** Wenxiao Zhao, Dong Liu, Kaiyi Xu, Feng Liu, Zhen Zhao, Fei Ben, Shu Wang, Wenhao Li, Yingnian Wu, Fenghua Ling, Haobo Li, and Lei Bai. **Affiliations:** Shanghai AI Laboratory, UCLA, and Tongji University.

2. **[PILOT in the Loop: Live Self-Improvement for Long-Horizon Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26530)** — Combines supervisor steering during an active run with persistent skills and memory reused in later runs; model weights remain frozen. **People:** Yang Xiao, Yusong Sun, Haoyi Wu, Wenyang Hui, Wen Da, Zhaokai Luo, Mu Chuan, Yao Hu, Wenjie Li, and Chengyue Jiang. **Affiliation listed:** AllSpark Team.

3. **[CoWork-X: Experience-Optimized Co-Evolution for Multi-Agent Collaboration System](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.05004)** — Couples fast skill execution within episodes with post-episode diagnosis and updates to a shared skill library. **People and affiliations:** Zexin Lin (CUHK Shenzhen; AutoGame Research), Jiachen Yu and Yujiu Yang (Tsinghua University), Haoyang Zhang and Yuzhao Li (AutoGame Research), Zhonghang Li (CUHK Shenzhen), Junjie Wang (Tsinghua; AutoGame Research), and Xiaoqiang Ji (CUHK Shenzhen; Shenzhen Institute of Artificial Intelligence and Robotics for Society).

4. **[Adaptation of Agentic AI: A Survey of Post-Training, Memory, and Skills](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.16301)** — A broader overview connecting parameter training, persistent memory, and reusable skills. **People include:** lead authors Pengcheng Jiang and Jiacheng Lin (UIUC), Zhiyi Shi (UIUC; Harvard), plus Yejin Choi (Stanford), Dawn Song (UC Berkeley), Jimeng Sun (UIUC; Keiji AI), and Jiawei Han (UIUC).

1. **[EAU: Environment-Agent-User Co-evolution for Training User-Centric Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16523)** — October 2026. A meta-agent adapts the environment, user simulator, and training configuration alongside policy learning. **People:** Min Cai (University of Alberta), Dan Zhang (National University of Singapore), Gao Xing and Libin Ma (Kuaishou Technology), Zhaohui Xu (independent researcher), and Xi Ye (University of Alberta / Amii).

2. **[SEAL: Synergistic Co-Evolution of Agents and Learning Environments](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.24426)** — May 2026. Uses diagnosed agent failures to jointly improve the policy and the environment’s tool guidance and feedback. **People:** Yihao Hu, Zhihao Wen, Xiujin Liu, Pan Wang, Xin Zhang, and Wei Wu. **Affiliations represented:** Ant Group, Westlake University, University of Michigan–Ann Arbor, and University of Science and Technology of China.

3. **[CoEvolve: Training LLM Agents via Agent-Data Mutual Evolution](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.15840)** — April 2026. Evolves training tasks using feedback from agent interactions, including uncertainty and forgetting. **People:** Shidong Yang, Ziyu Ma, Tongwen Huang, Yiming Hu, Yong Wang, and Xiangxiang Chu — all affiliated with AMAP, Alibaba Group.

4. **[GenEnv: Difficulty-Aligned Co-Evolution Between LLM Agents and Environment Simulators](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.19682)** — December 2025. Co-trains an agent and a simulator that generates tasks matched to the agent’s current abilities. **People:** Jiacheng Guo, Jiahao Qiu, and Mengdi Wang (Princeton); Ling Yang (Princeton / ByteDance Seed); Ke Shen (ByteDance Seed); Peter Chen (Columbia); Qixin Xiao and Xinzhe Juan (University of Michigan); Yinjie Wang (University of Chicago).

query: multi-turn reinforcement learning user simulation benchmarks
text:
1. **[LMRL Gym: Benchmarks for Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning with Language Models](https://lmrl-gym.github.io/)** — A close match: eight multi-turn tasks, with LLM-simulated conversation partners, online environments, and offline training datasets. **People:** Marwa Abdulhai, Isadora White, Charlie Snell, Charles Sun, Joey Hong, and Yuexiang Zhai (UC Berkeley); Kelvin Xu (Google DeepMind); Sergey Levine (both).

2. **[UserBench: An Interactive Gym Environment for User-Centric Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.22034v1)** — Benchmarks agents interacting with simulated users whose preferences emerge gradually, testing clarification and tool-assisted decisions. **People:** Cheng Qian (Salesforce AI Research and University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign); Heng Ji (UIUC); Zuxin Liu, Akshara Prabhakar, Zhiwei Liu, Jianguo Zhang, Haolin Chen, Weiran Yao, Shelby Heinecke, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, and Huan Wang (Salesforce AI Research).

4. **[Consistently Simulating Human Personas with Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.00222v1)** — An evaluation and training framework for persona consistency in simulated patients, students, and social partners. **People:** Marwa Abdulhai, Ryan Cheng, and Sergey Levine (UC Berkeley); Donovan Clay and Tim Althoff (University of Washington); Natasha Jaques (University of Washington and Google DeepMind).
